definition: The generation and presentation of data insights, metrics, and analytics in a structured format for decision-making.
extendedDefinition: Reporting is the structured presentation of data insights that supports decisions, ranging from scheduled operational summaries to interactive dashboards and regulatory filings. Good reporting turns raw activity into questions answered: which customers are at risk, where throughput fell, what initiatives returned value. Buyers should evaluate reporting on the questions the organization actually asks, not the number of chart types available, and should check whether standard reports can be modified without developer assistance. Data freshness matters as much as presentation: reports built on stale or incomplete data misdirect decisions, so source accuracy and update frequency belong in the evaluation. Distribution is another factor, whether automated schedules, exports, or role-based views reach the people who act on them. Organizations adopting new software should confirm that reporting covers their compliance obligations, since manual report assembly is a persistent hidden cost.
